title: The Role of Bacteriophages in Gut-Microbiome Regulation and Their Potential Application Against Antimicrobial-Resistant Infections: A Systematic Review
content: Phages specifically infect bacteria and play an important role in microbial ecology, host microbiome interactions and regulators of the gut microbiome. The mechanisms to selectively target bacterial pathogens has attracted growing interest as a potential strategy for managing antimicrobial-resistant infections. Besides, enabling them to target pathogenic bacteria limiting disruption of beneficial intestinal microbiota. This review aims to systematically evaluate the role of bacteriophages in gut microbiome regulation, mechanisms of interaction with bacterial communities, potential against antimicrobial-resistant pathogens, and their therapeutic, immunological and practical applications. A systematic literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ResearchGate, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Studies relevant to bacteriophage on gut microbiome interactions, antimicrobial resistance, gastrointestinal infections, immune regulation, inflammatory bowel disease, and therapeutic applications were considered. Study selection was conducted using predefined eligibility criteria and reported according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Beside identify 419 records around 105 studies met the inclusion criteria (24 reviews and commentaries, 9 clinical trials or cohorts, 13 case reports or compassionate-use reports, 19 preclinical animal studies, 21 in vitro or mechanistic studies, 14 metagenomic or observational studies and 5 regulatory or commercial records). The evidence synthesis will examine bacteriophage-mediated regulation of bacterial populations, selective pathogen targeting, interactions between phage resistance and antibiotic susceptibility, potential applications in gastrointestinal infections, immunological interactions, and microbiome-associated disease. However, improved phage characterization, phage therapy against AMR infection are beneficial, but large-scale randomized trials, standardized phage characteristics and long-term ecological and immunological studies are required before clinical use.
